title: Why a work message can feel like a threat

audience.who: office staff at a mid-size company, any role
audience.knows: what a racing heart before a tough email feels like; no physiology
audience.cares_about: staying clear-headed and kind when work gets tense

outcome: The next time a message spikes their stress, the viewer recognises the alarm for what it is and takes one slow pause before replying
through_line: Your body runs an old alarm built for physical danger; a tense message can set it off, and a short pause gives your thinking time to catch up

arc_plan.what: One worker opens a message marked urgent and her body reacts before she has finished reading it
Name it as the body's fast stress response, an alarm that prepares you to act
Show the alarm running inside her: the hormones named on screen, energy pushed to muscles, the slower jobs paused one by one
The alarm was made for a short physical threat; at a desk there is nothing to run from, and a hasty reply is the likely outcome
The same moment again, now with a pause: the alarm settles and she replies on purpose

must_cover.what: the fast stress response prepares the body for action
the hormones involved, named simply, as the knowledge sheet states them
some functions that are not urgent are turned down during the response
it evolved for short physical threats, and modern triggers can set it off too
one practical move: a short pause before replying to a message that triggered the alarm

must_avoid: medical advice, diagnosis or treatment claims
numbers or percentages of any kind
telling the viewer stress is bad or that they are doing it wrong
breathing techniques presented as a cure
blaming the sender of the message
more than one metaphor for the response
example_posture: One invented worker at a desk, clearly illustrative ('say'); an ordinary urgent message, never a named company or person.
visual_direction: A figure lit from inside as the alarm switches on, labels pinned to her body as each hormone is named, a status panel whose slower jobs switch off one per word, a burst behind her at the moment of alarm, then the same desk calm again; saturated colour fields that glow, something quietly alive in every frame.
voice_note: A calm colleague who has felt this too; plain words, no lecture, warm on the last line.
